name: Isobutyl chloroformate
description: Isobutyl chloroformate (CAS 543-27-1 ), commonly abbreviated as IBCF, is a reactive acylating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, specialty chemical manufacturing, and flavor chemistry. It functions as an activated carbonyl intermediate, enabling efficient coupling and protection reactions under mild conditions. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, IBCF is the reagent of choice for mixed anhydride peptide coupling, where it activates carboxylic acids for amide bond formation in API synthesis. This process is essential for creating complex molecular structures in modern medicine. Flavor and fragrance producers use it to synthesize isobutyl esters that contribute characteristic fruity notes to food and cosmetic formulations. These esters are highly valued for their aromatic profiles and stability in various consumer products. In fine chemical synthesis, it serves as a protecting group reagent for amines and alcohols, a step critical in multi-stage synthesis routes where selectivity is required. This allows chemists to manipulate specific functional groups without affecting others. Specialty polymer and agrochemical manufacturers also employ it as a carbonylating agent to introduce chloroformate functionality into target molecules. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial laboratories and large-scale production facilities. Isobutyl chloroformate is supplied as a clear, moisture-sensitive liquid, typically packaged under inert atmosphere to preserve reactivity. Proper handling and storage are necessary to maintain the chemical integrity of the product over time. It is available in technical and synthesis grades, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 97% to 99%+ for research and industrial use. These grades ensure that the material meets the rigorous demands of high-precision chemical engineering. Packaging options generally include small reagent quantities through to bulk drums for commercial-scale production.
